claims.text: A single-crystal insulating material can be used to study lattice heat conductivity when its heat transport is dominated by phonons and electronic contributions are minimal.
Undoped silicon is an example of an intrinsic semiconductor suitable for the proposed study.
MgO is an example of an insulating oxide suitable for the proposed study.
Controlled synthesis or post-treatment can introduce short-range-order precipitates without significantly altering the base lattice.
Thermal annealing or doping can encourage the formation of short-range order.
Phonon transport dominates from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures in the proposed material.
Controlled SRO precipitates can be distributed within a crystalline matrix.
The boundaries of SRO precipitates scatter phonons.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon lifetimes or scattering times.
Reduced phonon lifetimes lower lattice thermal conductivity.
Introducing SRO precipitates will measurably decrease lattice thermal conductivity relative to a pristine precipitate-free crystal.
The reduction in lattice thermal conductivity increases as precipitate density increases.
The proposed effect is expected only where phonon conduction predominates.
Electronic heat conduction in conductors or heavily doped semiconductors may mask or alter the thermal-conductivity trend caused by SRO precipitates.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity reduction depends on precipitate size, inter-precipitate spacing, and spatial distribution.
